_comment: Opinionated rule overrides for application security work. NOT YET LOADED — claude-code-hook reads its rules from src/rules.ts in v0. Once v0.2 lands rule-file loading (~/.agentgate/rules.json or AGENTGATE_RULES_FILE), this file will plug in.
name: security-agent-default
description: Opinionated overrides for safe AppSec / SecEng work on top of the built-in rule set.

tier_overrides._comment: Security work is high-trust. Default everything to 'ask'. Quiet allow-list below for the silent investigative tools. Intentionally stricter than devops-agent-default (which sets low='off') — security findings act on credentials, identity, and data, so the cost of a silent action is higher.

always_allow: _comment: read-only investigative tool-call patterns that are safe in this agent's context
always_ask: _comment: things that even auto-policy should never auto-approve
always_deny: _comment_truth: pattern-based deny lists are policy signaling, not a security control. A determined caller can defeat any string match with shell tricks (var expansion, base64, intermediate scripts). The real boundary is the persona + the human-approval step + scope authorization. This list exists to (a) make the default posture visible, (b) catch unintentional invocations, (c) give the agent a clear pointer that these patterns should be refused with explanation rather than silently translated into an approval prompt.
_comment_destructive_system: never allow these even with approval — they have no legitimate use in this agent's scope

_comment_offense_default: signal that offensive tooling should be refused by default. The agent's persona is the real gate here — it refuses when scope is not authorized and explains. An authorized pentest engagement should load a separate, scope-bounded rule pack (planned for v0.2 multi-pack support), not weaken this one.
_comment_payloads: signal refusal for common reverse-shell / persistence shapes. Not bypass-proof.
always_redact: _comment: patterns the agent must never echo into chat / logs / commits even if it sees them

approver_constraints._comment: Constraints on who can approve what (planned for v0.2 with multi-tenant)
